title: Legal Triage I/O
description: Input/output contract for function 124. The model's own job is narrow -- classify one already-produced pending OptionCard's text against the three-tier rule prompt.md states, name the rule, and (for AMBER) draft the specific softening. Assembling the legal.amber / legal.sensitive_statement OptionCard, and sweeping the pending-card queue in the first place, is orchestrator code (services/orchestrator/orchestrator/dispatch.py's legal_triage_sweep_handler), not this model's job -- the same split every other drafting/classifying handler in this file uses. NOT wired as a synchronous gate in front of every card-producing handler (Fn 116/115/118/127/128/129 among them) -- prompt.md's own words ('every option payload passes through you before the card is emitted') describe that end state, but retrofitting it into six existing, shipped call sites is exactly the kind of shared-mechanism change this repo's own hard rules say needs auditing across every one of them, not a one-PR addition. Runs instead as an independent sweep over whatever is currently pending, mirroring Fn 129's own relationship to Fn 128.

text.description: The pending card's title/decision_question/options[].summary/rationale, concatenated -- everything a ratifier would actually read.

rule_cited.description: Which specific prompt.md rule triggered this tier -- logged to context_summary so the evaluator can audit calibration.

softened_text.description: AMBER only: the specific softening drafted for the 'publish with softening' option. null for GREEN/RED.
